newsitem.title: UK: UK road deaths fall to record low.
newsitem.headline: UK road deaths fall to record low.

text.p: The number of people killed or seriously injured in road accidents in Britain has fallen to the lowest level since records began in 1926, the government said on Thursday.
In 1996 there were 3,598 deaths compared to 3,621 the year before. Serious injuries were down two percent from 1995 levels.
Fatalities had fallen 36 percent from the 1981-85 average, while serious injuries were down 40 percent, despite the fact that overall traffic had risen by half.

Transport officials attributed the decrease to increased public awareness of the dangers of drinking and driving, compulsory use of seat belts, improved driver training and enforcement of lower speed limits.
